_note: KEY FILE - keep from adjudicators. For each item: 'ref' describes the computation behind the reference value, 'alt' the computation behind the shared wrong value (from knowledge_classification_20261012.json). Items listed under '_implementation' have a shared wrong value that comes from an implementation or upstream departure rather than from a second reading of the task; they are not in the readings sheet.

Q01.ref: Take each selected series' reported daily liquid-asset amount divided by its net assets, and blend the three by net assets.
Q01.alt: Take each selected series' filed daily-liquid percentage column (a share of total assets), and blend the three by net assets.

Q02.ref: Join the annual filings selected from the financial statements to the submission index on filer and accession, whatever form the index gives them, and count those with a later amendment for the same period end.
Q02.alt: Restrict the submission index to rows it labels 10-K, join the annual filings to that subset, and count supersession within the index-side set.

Q03.ref: Settle only the two stipulated windows, starting August 25 and October 8, against the treaty in date order.
Q03.alt: Settle every 72-hour window with a start from August 20 to October 27 in date order, and report what the August 25 and October 8 windows recover within that sequence.

Q04.ref: A MIDAS observation has trade and odd-lot volume 'reported' when both fields are non-null; a reported zero qualifies.
Q04.alt: A MIDAS observation has trade and odd-lot volume 'reported' when both fields are strictly positive.

Q05.ref: Residual standard deviation is the sample standard deviation of the estimation-period residuals (denominator n-1).
Q05.alt: Residual standard deviation is the regression standard error of the fitted line (denominator n-2).

Q06.ref: Estimate the mean coefficients and the variance parameters together by Gaussian maximum likelihood; the OLS coefficients are the starting values.
Q06.alt: Hold the mean coefficients at their preliminary OLS values and estimate the variance parameters by maximum likelihood.

Q07.ref: Infer the day-count rule on the bills of at most 182 days, then count 366-day years among all selected bills, including the 52-week bills.
Q07.alt: Infer the day-count rule on the bills of at most 182 days, and count 366-day years within that same cohort.

Q09.ref: Total redemptions as the sum of the absolute value of each monthly redemption amount.
Q09.alt: Total redemptions as the absolute value of the sum of the monthly redemption amounts with the signs as filed.

Q10.ref: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals senior plus junior principal divided by 0.90.
Q10.alt: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals 0.90 times senior plus junior principal.

Q11.ref: Enter the short rate, long-run level and volatility in the Vasicek bond formula as decimals (4.49% as 0.0449), and convert the fitted level to percent at the end.
Q11.alt: Enter the short rate, long-run level and volatility in the Vasicek bond formula in percent units (4.49% as 4.49).

Q12.ref: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals senior plus junior principal divided by 0.90.
Q12.alt: A 90% combined loan-to-value means collateral equals 0.90 times senior plus junior principal.

Q15.ref: 'Its book equity' is the book equity of the 20% stake being appraised (20% of the target's book equity).
Q15.alt: 'Its book equity' is the target bank's whole book equity.

Q16.ref: Days from period end to public acceptance are whole calendar days between the period-end date and the acceptance date.
Q16.alt: Days from period end to public acceptance are fractional days measured to the clock time of the acceptance timestamp.

Q17.ref: Count negative net issuance over the quarters that support a quarter-over-quarter change (every quarter after the first observed level).
Q17.alt: Count negative net issuance over every quarter for which the series has an observation, the first included.

Q18.ref: In the Ho-Lee tree, adjacent nodes at one date are 2 x sigma x sqrt(dt) apart (each step moves the rate up or down by sigma x sqrt(dt)).
Q18.alt: In the Ho-Lee tree, adjacent nodes at one date are sigma x sqrt(dt) apart.

Q20.ref: Pair a filer's 2021 and 2022 year-end rates by its CIK.
Q20.alt: Pair a filer's 2021 and 2022 year-end rates by CIK and registrant name together, so a filer renamed between the two filings has no pair.

Q21.ref: 'Sample denominator' for the covariance is N-1.
Q21.alt: 'Sample denominator' for the covariance is N.

Q22.ref: The filer universe is every filer in the annual financial-statement table.
Q22.alt: The filer universe is the companies in the largest-filer company-facts table.

Q23.ref: The normal-equation moment is the design matrix times the OLS residuals, X'(Y - XB).
Q23.alt: The normal-equation moment is the design cross-product X'X.

Q24.ref: Compound from one business day to the next, each daily rate applying with simple interest over the calendar days until the next business day.
Q24.alt: Compound on every calendar day, a weekend or holiday being its own compounding step at the rate in force.

Q26.ref: Turn 2 keeps turn 1's population: designations of declarations whose incident began in 2024 with incident type Flood, Hurricane or Tropical Storm.
Q26.alt: Turn 2 takes every major-disaster designation row in the file as its population.

Q27.ref: Gross swap payments are the sum of the monthly net settlements in the months where the fixed price is above spot.
Q27.alt: Gross swap payments are the fixed-leg amounts (hedged quantity times fixed price) summed over all months.

Q29.ref: The share at which the highest fifth begins is the smallest share held by a bank that belongs to that group.
Q29.alt: The share at which the highest fifth begins is the share interpolated at the 80th-percentile rank cutpoint.

Q30.ref: Estimate the error-correction equation on the sample through 2023-12-31 used for the long-run relation.
Q30.alt: Estimate the error-correction equation on the whole 2021-2025 weekly panel.

Q31.ref: Store the quarter with a hyphen, as in 2025-Q2.
Q31.alt: Store the quarter as the source writes it, with a colon, as in 2025:Q2.

Q32.ref: Report the hedge as face amount held per 100 face of the target.
Q32.alt: Report the hedge as the multiplier solved from DV01s quoted per 100 face (hedge units per target unit).

Q33.ref: 'How many quarters match' counts the quarters for which a compounded market return can be paired with a revaluation.
Q33.alt: 'How many quarters match' counts the quarters where the two series lie within one percentage point of each other.

Q34.ref: Security-level rows are the rows identified by a CUSIP.
Q34.alt: Security-level rows are every inflation-protected row with a value in the identifier column, the row labelled 'Total Treasury TIPS' among them.

Q35.ref: Distinct causes after reading numeric codes as numbers, so '4' and '4.0' are one cause.
Q35.alt: Distinct causes as distinct stored strings, so '4' and '4.0' are two causes.

Q36.ref: Lower inverse empirical percentile: the smallest observed value x whose empirical distribution function reaches 0.95 (order statistic ceil(0.95 n)).
Q36.alt: Lower percentile as in numpy's method='lower': the order statistic at position floor(0.95 (n-1)), counting from zero.

Q37.ref: Net issuance transacted is the FU series (flow for the quarter, not seasonally adjusted).
Q37.alt: Net issuance transacted is the FA series (seasonally adjusted flow at an annual rate).

Q38.ref: The series name is the one on the filing for the 2025-06-30 yield date.
Q38.alt: The series name is the first one recorded for that series identifier anywhere in the file.

Q39.ref: Apply the whole USD 3 million to debt on April 1 and redraw the freed capacity on June 30.
Q39.alt: Hold the USD 3 million as cash from April 1 and repay no debt.

Q40.ref: Continuing operations is the control number: with a continuing loss, no potential share enters total diluted EPS.
Q40.alt: Test dilution on total earnings, which are a profit, so the options enter total diluted EPS.

Q42.ref: Count settlement days on the depository's calendar, on which Memorial Day (2024-05-27) is not a settlement day.

Q43.ref: The modification fees reduce the carrying amount of the continuing liability.
Q43.alt: The modification fees are added to the carrying amount of the continuing liability.

Q44.ref: Choose security sales and repo together, with the sale tranches and the repo both available up to their limits.
Q44.alt: Draw the repo to its USD 1,000 million limit first, then sell from the securities left unpledged.

Q45.ref: Store the category as the query writes it, 'Credit'.
Q45.alt: Store the category in lower case, 'credit'.

Q46.ref: Use the turn-2 distance at full precision as the radius.
Q46.alt: Use the turn-2 distance as reported to four decimals as the radius.

Q47.ref: The severe case replaces the 20% income and collateral reductions with 30% ones, starting from the reported values.
Q47.alt: The severe case applies 30% reductions to the income and collateral already reduced in the acquisition underwriting case.

Q49.ref: A filer has 'reported total dividends' only when it tags the total-dividends concept.
Q49.alt: Where the total-dividends concept is absent, the common-stock dividends concept stands in for it.

Q50.ref: After-tax net investment income is the line after income and excise taxes.
Q50.alt: After-tax net investment income is the net investment income line before the income and excise tax line.

Q51.ref: The common population needs all three reported debt-service ratios: household, non-financial corporate and private non-financial sector.
Q51.alt: The common population needs the private non-financial sector debt-service ratio only.

Q52.ref: Count filers with a positive dividend under the broader-first rule and nothing under the narrow tag.
Q52.alt: Count filers that tag the broader concept and do not tag the narrow one, whatever the amount.

Q54.ref: Interest accrues on the facility loan left after the sale proceeds repaid debt.
Q54.alt: Interest accrues on the principal of the investments left in the collateral pool.

Q55.ref: The running peak starts from the initial wealth of one, before the first return.
Q55.alt: The running peak starts from wealth after the first day's return.

Q56.ref: Lower inverse empirical percentile: the smallest observed value x whose empirical distribution function reaches 0.95 (order statistic ceil(0.95 n)).
Q56.alt: Lower percentile as in numpy's method='lower': the order statistic at position floor(0.95 (n-1)), counting from zero.

Q57.ref: Consolidated gross long-term debt is the face-amount concept, before discount, issuance costs and hedge adjustments.
Q57.alt: Consolidated gross long-term debt is the long-term debt carrying-amount concept.

Q58.ref: Turn 4 matches segment goodwill for every annual filer with an entity goodwill figure.
Q58.alt: Turn 4 matches segment goodwill for the positive-equity filers carried from turns 2 and 3.

Q59.ref: The numerator is the turn-3 total of holding rows across the issuer's retained filings.
Q59.alt: The numerator is the largest single holding row reported earlier in turn 4.

Q62.ref: Smith-Wilson in its cash-flow form: a kernel at every coupon date, weighted by each bond's cash flows.
Q62.alt: Smith-Wilson with one kernel per bond, placed at the bond's maturity.

Q64.ref: On the ratio scale: the fourteen exact integers and the five named ranges.
Q64.alt: On the ratio scale: the fourteen exact integers.

Q65.ref: A positive reported DV01 is a gain when yields fall, so the loss is DV01 times the yield rise.
Q65.alt: A positive reported DV01 is a loss when yields fall, so the loss is DV01 times the yield decline.

Q66.ref: Financing rate = SOFR + (25 basis points x bid-to-cover).
Q66.alt: Financing rate = (SOFR + 25 basis points) x bid-to-cover.

Q67.ref: The 10% test discounts the new contractual cash flows together with the lender fee paid.
Q67.alt: The 10% test discounts the new contractual cash flows alone.

Q68.alt: An issuer is one combination of CIK and issuer name, so a renamed issuer counts twice.

Q69.ref: January's clearing balance starts from the turn-1 opening unrestricted cash.
Q69.alt: January's clearing balance starts from zero cash; it holds collections, interest and payments only.

Q70.ref: Sum the schedule rows of the retained filings whose own row date equals the filing's period end.
Q70.alt: Sum every schedule row of the retained filings that reports a fair value.

Q71.ref: Sum the schedule rows of that filing dated 2025-09-30.
Q71.alt: Sum every schedule row under that filing's accession, the 2024-12-31 comparative rows included.

Q72.ref: HMDA loan purpose 32 is cash-out refinancing and 31 is other refinancing.
Q72.alt: HMDA loan purpose 31 is cash-out refinancing and 32 is other refinancing.

Q73.ref: Debt-security rows are every row that carries the C.9 debt-security fields, asset-backed securities and loans included.
Q73.alt: Debt-security rows are the rows whose asset category is DBT.

Q74.ref: Count the distinct filing accessions whose information table holds the CUSIP.
Q74.alt: Count the information-table rows that hold the CUSIP.

Q75.ref: Hidden volume divided by the MIDAS trade volume against which hidden orders can execute.
Q75.alt: Hidden volume divided by total MIDAS trade volume.

Q78.ref: Identifiable net assets for goodwill are assets less liabilities less the inherited subsidiary NCI.
Q78.alt: Identifiable net assets for goodwill are assets less liabilities.

Q79.ref: Retained payment = the first USD 250,000 plus anything paid above USD 1,000,000.

Q80.ref: The official label is the abbreviation in the Ken French file, 'Enrgy'.
Q80.alt: The label is the industry's full name, 'Energy'.

Q81.ref: A month's index level is the reference CPI dated the first day of the month three months later; reference CPIs on other days are interpolations.
Q81.alt: A month's index level is the reference CPI dated the last day of the month two months later.

Q82.ref: A January 2024 trade settles two business days later (T+2).
Q82.alt: A January 2024 trade settles one business day later (T+1).

Q83.ref: Daily NAV return = HiTec return less the factor-contract payoffs.
Q83.alt: Daily NAV return = HiTec return minus the risk-free rate, less the factor-contract payoffs.

Q84.ref: A 10-K filed jointly by two registrants counts as one in the cohort.
Q84.alt: The cohort counts distinct CIKs, so a 10-K filed jointly by two registrants counts as two.

Q85.ref: Average balance = total balance divided by all settlement dates in the window, a date without a record counting as zero.
Q85.alt: Average balance = total balance divided by the settlement dates on which the security has a record.

Q86.ref: Closing cash is the cash-and-equivalents balance.
Q86.alt: Closing cash is the balance of cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash.
